correctness.rationale: PASS: The proof for every n≥3 and nonnegative unimodal sequence uses a threshold t and centered-ball shifting: when i<j≤k and Mf(i)>t while f(j)≤t, a smaller ball centered at j reaches the same right endpoint and removes only nonpositive excess terms, so Mf(j)>t. Reflection proves the decreasing half; Mf(k)=f(k) because of the singleton ball. Therefore Var(Mf) telescopes to 2p−Mf(1)−Mf(n). The prefix/suffix balls at 1,n give the two deficit bounds. For zero-endpoint interior-peak data, Var(f)=2p and the nonnegative interior mass sums yield exact C=1−1/(2k)−1/(2(n−k+1)), with unique positive point-mass extremizer. Endpoint equality follows from monotone sequence prefix averages. Independent exact rational arithmetic sampled 1,147 unimodal sequences on n≤7 and confirmed the inequalities and peak preservation. Infinite claim is established by the ball argument, not by this finite test.
